body: May important counter-signal sa oil-risk story: 17 million barrels reportedly passed the Strait of Hormuz on Monday — the highest daily crude transit since wartime restrictions cut flows. So Brent near $96 is not clean proof na lumalala ang physical supply shortage; part of the price can still be geopolitical risk premium. Translation: huwag gawing thermometer ng actual disruption ang oil price lang. If transit keeps normalizing while Brent stays high, the story shifts from ‘shortage’ toward ‘risk premium + inflation expectations.’

sources.title: US energy secretary says 17 million barrels of oil transited Strait of Hormuz on Monday

claims.text: U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said 17 million barrels of crude oil transited the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, the highest daily volume since the Iran war had reduced flows.
claims.basis: Reuters report quoting the U.S. Energy Secretary.

claims.text: If physical transit continues recovering while Brent remains elevated, a larger share of the oil price may reflect geopolitical and inflation risk premium rather than worsening physical shortage.
claims.basis: Calibration inference comparing physical throughput with elevated market pricing.
